residual: P2: The pin reads and asserts over the ENTIRE CHANGELOG, but scripts/release.py rolls the [Unreleased] section into a frozen dated section inside the same file (re.subn on '^## \[Unreleased\]' inserts a new empty Unreleased above it). Once this entry is released it becomes immutable history, yet test_the_changelog_open_question_count_matches_the_register keeps asserting that history's count equals the LIVE register's. The first time a question is settled and platform-probes.md drops to 'Two questions', the pin goes red against a published entry that was accurate when written, and the only fixes are rewriting release history or deleting the pin. test_the_changelog_retracted_untested_framing_is_gone has the same whole-file scope: it forbids the string 'is one-shot per session is NOT established' anywhere in the CHANGELOG forever, including in a future entry that legitimately quotes the retracted claim while describing this very correction. Separately, CHANGELOG_OPEN_COUNT_RE.search returns only the FIRST match, so after a roll a newer entry's count is the one checked and older restatements are unchecked - defensible for history, but it means the pin silently stops guarding the text it was written for.

P3: PROBES_NUMBERED_ITEM_RE counts every '^N. ' line in the whole of platform-probes.md, not just the open-question list, so the cross-check between the register's spelled-out word and its list length is coupled to the file having exactly one numbered list. It has exactly one today (lines 81/87/89, which I counted on disk: 3 matches, matching 'Three'), so the check is sound as merged. Adding any unrelated numbered list to that register turns test_the_register_word_matches_its_numbered_list red without the open-question count having drifted at all. The implementer disclosed this and documented it in the class docstring; I confirmed the failure direction is a visible false red, never a silent pass, so it is a maintenance trap rather than a correctness hole.

P3: The count assertions are deliberately derived from both files so the pin never needs an edit, but CHANGELOG_TOPICS is three hard-coded literals with no link to the register's numbered items. When a question is settled, both files' counts drop together and the count tests stay green, while test_the_changelog_names_each_open_question fails on a stale literal for a question that correctly no longer exists - the exact 'unedited pin is as stale as the prose it guards' failure the docstring says the design avoids. The failure is a visible red, and deriving topics mechanically is real work (the two files word the same question differently: 'Does Ctrl+C route through `Stop`?' vs 'whether Ctrl+C routes through `Stop`'), so this is a scoped caveat, not a defect in what shipped.

P2: The new TestCase's docstring documents an honest limit for the numbered-item-count's file-wide scope, but omits the comparable and arguably more fragile limitation that CHANGELOG_TOPICS is three hard-coded literal strings with no mechanical link back to platform-probes.md's numbered questions -- so the docstring's framing ('Both counts are read out of the two files... an unedited pin is as stale as the prose it guards') reads as broader drift-proofing than the code actually delivers for per-question content, not just the count.

P3: CHANGELOG_INSTALL_VERSION_LIMIT is a module-scope name added by the implementer that is not listed in Task 2's Interfaces > Produces list (which enumerates CHANGELOG_MD, WORD_TO_INT, CHANGELOG_OPEN_COUNT_RE, PROBES_OPEN_COUNT_RE, PROBES_NUMBERED_ITEM_RE, CHANGELOG_TOPICS, CHANGELOG_RETRACTED_FRAMING, and the TestCase class only). It is a reasonable, well-justified quality-gate-driven hoist (self-disclosed by the implementer as a deviation), but it is unplanned scope per the plan's explicit Produces contract.
